children: The Yobe State Government has commenced discussions with Russian investment company, Legion Investment Moscow, on a proposed gas-powered electricity plant to power its Agro-Industrial Zone.
The plant is proposed to provide reliable power for agro-processing, manufacturing, storage, cold-chain facilities and other businesses in the zone.
Mamman Mohammed, Director-General, Press and Media Affairs to Governor Mai Mala Buni, disclosed this on his Facebook page.
He said the Russian company’s delegation, led by Mr Leonid Khasiev, met the governor on Monday ahead of technical engagements and inspection of proposed project sites.
According to Mohammed, the visit was part of an investment and technical assessment of the proposed project.
Khasiev, accompanied by the company’s technical consultant, Mr Rasim Azimov, said the delegation was in Yobe to assess the technical and investment requirements of the project.
He said the team would inspect the proposed sites and engage relevant authorities on the planned energy solution for the Agro-Industrial Zone.

The engagement is part of the state government’s efforts to move agriculture beyond primary production by developing facilities for production, aggregation, processing, storage, logistics and market access.
Governor Buni said the engagement would help the state attract international investors and strategic technical partners to support its development priorities.

Buni appreciated Legion Investment Moscow for its interest in Yobe, saying the proposed partnership could help realise the Agro-Industrial Zone, create jobs, promote value addition and attract investment into the agricultural sector.

“Yobe State remains committed to building strategic partnerships that will unlock the economic potential of its agricultural resources and position the state as an attractive destination for agro-industrial investment,” the governor said.

title: ZAWYA: Nigeria: Yobe to power agro-industrial zone with Russian gas plant
